content: cslib#435 adds some useful grind annotations, a lemma for bind and pure composition and a Coe for FreeM.liftM. While they were originally made in the context of cslib#372 by Eric, I believe they are independently useful to CSLib. The PR passes CI.
The new lemmas here will probably conflict with cslib#417.

I'm not entirely convinced by the Coe instance; in your PR I recall that it didn't actually fire in many of the places you wanted it too. Could you put the Coe instance in its own PR, with tests that exercise it?
It didn't fire in one place because the underlying parameter/index type wasn't clear.
I use it everywhere else. I also use it in cslib#416 and cslib#429 which add TM and circuit models

In any case, my reason for making this PR is to consolidate my PRs and other branches related to Prog into one downstream repository called Algolean (pun fully intended) so that I can continue working on it for now.
and PRing this allows me to preserve my mergeSort proofs
To be clear I'm not opposed to the new lemmas necessarily, I'm just wondering if I should try to get that PR over the line first.
But the lemmas are certainly orthogonal to the coercion, and so make more sense in separate PRs
The coercion works in almost every case. I don't know the best course of action there. My PR is basically what you added to cslib#372 in February, plus the coercion

Shreyas Srinivas said:

I don't know the best course of action there

It is what I wrote above:

Eric Wieser said:

Could you put the Coe instance in its own PR, with tests that exercise it?
okay. If that helps. But what tests should I build? The best breaking examples I know come from my Arith query.
cslib#435 does not have the coe instance now

But what tests should I build?

Any test will do for now. Your PR adding Coe should at minimum add some code that uses the coercion, in order to demo why we want it (and ensure that the feature isn't removed by accident)
